description.narrative: Securing multiple ecosystems benefit through Sustainable Land Management (SLM) in the productive but degraded landscapes of South Africa

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

comment.narrative:
1.1. a) Karoo: 500,000 hectares of degraded land b) Olifants: 41,300 hectares of degraded land c) Eastern Cape: 11,733 hectares of degraded land
2.1. Score: 2 (there is some capacity for design and implementation of SLM practices, but this is nascent)
3.1. 9,081 hectares of degraded spekboomveld 3.2. There is currently no simplified methodology for for calculation of certified emissions reductions/carbon credits from spekboomveld restoration 3.3. No land users in the Baviaanskloof are currently part of a Programme of Activities/Grouped Project
4.1. There is currently little integration of SLM practices into national and sub-national strategies for development and land-use planning. Where these do exist, they are seldom based on up-do-date scientific knowledge on SLM best practices and do not always incorporate a diverse range of stakeholder priorities. 4.2. Current agricultural and related policies do not incentivise the implementation of SLM practices. Consequently, land users are unable to take advantage of opportunities for implementation of SLM practices in currently degraded landscapes.

1.1. Implement Small Grants in all three project landscapes (Karoo, Eastern Cape and Olifants) landscapes to out-scale Sustainable Land Management (SLM) better practices 1.2. Active restoration of degraded landscapes in all project landscapes 1.3. Landscapes strategies piloted and rolled out by bringing in sustainable land management best practices 1.4. Capacity and Skills Assessment in project landscapes to align capacity building initiatives from local to national level
2.1. Simple and cheaper methodology developed and tested to determine carbon levels for carbon sequestration 2.2. Study, engage with stakeholders and determine the economic feasibility of opportunities posed by the Carbon Market for farmers, especially related to spekboom planting
3.1. Land degradation and SLM related training and awareness workshops in all landscapes 3.2. Project website and knowledge management system developed for project related activities and information and knowledge generated

1.1. Small Grants for all projects were approved and are in process of implementation in Karoo, Eastern Cape (Machubeni) and Olifants landscapes. Implementation not completed yet 1.2. Active restoration is happening in all project landscapes but final targets have not been achieved yet 1.3. Landscape strategies not completed in all landscapes but sustainable land management best practices have been included in restoration work in all landscapes 1.4. Process has started but not yet completed in all project landscapes
2.1. Methodology completed and documented 2.2. Study completed, engagement with stakeholders still underway
3.1. SLM related training has been conducted in all project landscapes – ongoing process 3.2. Project website complete, busy populating with data and information. Knowledge management system under design, not yet completed.

1.1. a) Karoo: At least 50 000 hectares under SLM practices b) Olifants: 16,000 hectares under SLM practices c) Eastern Cape: 1,300 ha under SLM practices
2.1. Score: at least 4 (there is widespread but not comprehensive capacity for design and implementation of SLM practices)
3.1. At least 1,000 hectares of degraded spekboomveld is restored 3.2. Government endorses a simplified methodology for calculation of certified emissions reductions/carbon credits from spekboomveld restoration 3.3. At least 30 land users in the Baviaanskloof sign an MoU to participate as proponents in a Programme of Activities/Grouped Project
4.1. A strategy for integrating SLM into development and land-use planning has been developed and implemented at the national and sub-national levels. 4.2. A comprehensive set of policy recommendations that mainstream long-term SLM objectives into policies related to inter alia agriculture, rangeland management, biodiversity, soil and water conservation and land reform

1.1. These are work in progress, progress to date are as follow: a) Karoo: 18 686ha of 50 000 ha target. c) Eastern Cape Machubeni: 1131.05 ha of 1300 ha
2.1. Score for capacity and skills development at 3.5 at this stage
3.1. 892 ha completed of 1000 ha of degraded spekboomveld to be rehabilitated 3.2. Methodology completed, engagement with Government has started to endorse the simplified methodology 3.3. Negotiations are ongoing to involve farmers of Baviaanskloof (Baviaanskloof Bewaria) in a Carbon Grouped Project. Initial indications are that we would not reach 30 farmers to willingly participate in the process. There are only limited farmers in the Baviaanskloof.
4.1. Involvement and inputs of GEF 5 UNDP PMU in UNDP driven Ecological Life Support Areas (ELSA) project for South Africa. Agro ecology and SLM was imbedded into this process to ensure prioritization and planning at national and sub-national levels and to inform strategies for development and land-use planning. 4.2. Policy recommendations is collected as the project continue for the different project landscapes and will be collated into a knowledge product towards the end of the project
